statement: Main experimental confounder: the context regime necessarily adds triples/tokens per supervision example, so any accuracy gain may reflect a larger supervision/context budget rather than passage-context relevance. Because the literature disagrees on whether more context helps (SG-RAG MOT: merging overlapping subgraphs helps) or hurts (DrKGC: overly long inputs add noise), the isolated-vs-context comparison must match the number of examples and total tokens and include an equal-length irrelevant-triples control.

evidence.quote: While graph paths or subgraphs can be encoded as text prompts, overly long inputs introduce noise and increase computational costs.
We also find out that merging (up to some point) highly overlapping subgraphs and defining an order among the triplets helps the LLM to generate more precise answers.
